answer: The hollow multiplier is published, charged in harbor, and pearl lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 4953 identities would post 2699 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
